angularDiameterSource: No angular diameter is measured: at 112 pc the star would be 0.10 mas across, below any interferometer's reach. This value is the record's radius, 1.26 solar radii from Keppler et al. (2018, Table 1), at the Gaia DR3 distance.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 source 6110141563309613056: parallax 8.8975 +/- 0.0191 mas (RUWE 1.39), inverted to 112.39 pc with no zero-point correction.
radiusSource: Radius 1.26 +/- 0.15 solar radii from Keppler et al. (2018, A&A 617, A44; arXiv:1806.11568), Table 1, from the luminosity 0.35 L_sun and effective temperature 3972 K at 113.4 pc: 876,582 km at 695700 km per solar radius (the Gaia DR3 distance, 112.39 pc, is 0.9% nearer; the radius is not rescaled). GM from the dynamical stellar mass 0.952 +0.032/-0.028 solar masses that Trevascus et al. (2025, Table 3, "Stable (incl. N-body)") fit together with the planets' orbits, times the JPL solar GM 132712440041.93938 km^3/s^2. presentationUp: the display axis (celestial north at the star) is up; the star's spin axis has no measured direction on the sky.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Keppler et al. (2018, A&A 617, A44), Table 1: 3972 +/- 36 K from the optical spectrum of Pecaut & Mamajek (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.11568
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the dynamical mass 0.952 solar masses of Trevascus et al. (2025, Table 3) and the radius 1.26 solar radii of Keppler et al. (2018, Table 1), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.22.
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of PDS 70 (pscomppars): spectral type K7, from Keppler et al. 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...617A..44K/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, CD-40 8434: main object type TT*, T Tauri Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of PDS 70 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.11 dex, from Swastik et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....161..114S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of PDS 70 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.45593, from Keppler et al. 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...617A..44K/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of PDS 70 (pscomppars): age 0.008 Gyr, from Wang et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....161..148W/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/AJ/165/164/table2 (Tull RVels, rotation periods and Inclinations), column Prot: 3.03 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place. The middle of 5 catalogued periods, 5 of them within 20% of it

projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of PDS 70 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 17.27 km/s, from Swastik et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....161..114S/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (1.26 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.821. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.
rotationPeriodMeasuredSource: Measured in this project from the TESS mission's own 2-minute light curves of sectors 11 and 102 (packages/telescope-cli/src/archives/tess/reduce.mts), by the method and criteria of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138): 3.06 d, the light swinging by 14% as the star turns

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius in the shared neutral gray; the photosphere of a giant star is not a solid surface and its limb is not sharp.
